turns.content: For ds^2=32(dx^2+dy^2)/(4-x^2-y^2) on x^2+y^2<4, write the metric tensor, its determinant, and the area element.
Transform the area integral for the coordinate disk of radius 2 into polar coordinates.
Analyze convergence of the radial improper integral as the coordinate radius approaches 2.
For truncated disks of radius R<2, determine the behavior of their area as R approaches 2 from below and identify the divergence type.
Why do the finite angular range and exclusion of the singular boundary circle not make the improper area finite?
Report the area of the radius-2 coordinate disk in the extended sense and justify it from the boundary behavior.
